examples.name: Failure
examples.note: A literal that does not match returns false.

examples.name: Sequence and alternatives
examples.note: A sequence; default parsing skips intervening whitespace.

examples.name: Alternatives
examples.note: Alternatives are ordered; the first successful branch wins.

examples.name: Nested rules
examples.note: A nested block is a rule sequence with its own alternatives.

examples.name: Repetition
examples.note: some means one or more; any/opt are also supported.

examples.name: Numeric repetition
examples.note: A number before a rule means exact count; two numbers mean min and max.

examples.name: skip / to / thru / end
examples.note: thru searches and consumes its target; to leaves it unconsumed.

examples.name: to target
examples.note: to seeks to b without consuming it; the following literal consumes it.

examples.name: Character set
examples.note: A charset string uses byte ranges; matching is case-sensitive.

examples.name: copy capture
examples.note: copy captures the source slice matched by its rule.

examples.name: none and end
examples.note: none succeeds without consuming; end matches end-of-input.
